{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-12T06:09:38.198610+00:00","domain":"general topology","id":"claim_ff61ff48cce572f4f7d51c7a320ea48eadc31611bdd1fdfe4cc31d52318be257","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For A a subset of a topological space (X, tau), the subspace (relative) topology on A is tau_A = { A intersect U : U in tau }: its open sets are the intersections with A of open sets of X, and likewise its closed sets are the intersections with A of closed sets of X. This is a topology - it contains A and empty, and the identities (A intersect U1) intersect (A intersect U2) = A intersect (U1 intersect U2) and union of (A intersect U_i) = A intersect (union U_i) give closure under finite intersections and arbitrary unions. It is the coarsest topology making the inclusion i: A -> X continuous, since i is continuous for a topology sigma on A iff A intersect U is sigma-open for every U in tau, i.e. iff tau_A is contained in sigma. Universal property: for any space Z, a map f: Z -> A is continuous iff the composite Z -> A -> X is continuous - the property that characterizes the subspace topology.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.494719+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ff77c1f088d0475912596d1b0474b612c2f8a2bac619ac99a18bb828c033a5d2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 26 (Fixed spectrum and fixed diagonal version) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:fixed-spectrum-fixed-diagonal}
Let \(w>0\) and \(u\geq 0\), and let
\[
        X=wG+uD,
\]
where \(G\) is a GUE matrix and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) is
fixed.  Let
\[
        \lambda=\spec(X),
        \qquad
        a=\diag(X).
\]
For \(1\leq k\leq n\), let \(\lambda^{(k)}\) be the ordered eigenvalue vector
of the \(k\times k\) northwest principal minor of \(X\), and write
\[
        \Gamma=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(n)}).
\]
Then, conditional on both
\[
        \spec(X)=\lambda
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \diag(X)=a,
\]
the minor process \(\Gamma\) is uniformly distributed, with respect to
Lebesgue measure, on the Gelfand-Tsetlin fiber
\[
        \GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}.
\]
Equivalently, its conditional density is
\[
        \frac{1}{|\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}|}
        \mathbf 1_{\{\Gamma\in \GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}\}} .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-02T00:34:53.678977+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_ff8cb4d1ac13756ca669cda475cfdca34bc188f7da0f7cab4d61292f12bb2424","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In mathematics, Minkowski's theorem is the statement that every convex set in which is symmetric with respect to the origin and which has volume greater than contains a non-zero integer point. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:29:21.897686+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ff8cc750a9b1846790835cfd7b86daedc2a493c8291ee04b1299a1fd15aad4db","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.00449, 'First-order phase transitions in the hard-core model'] \\label[definition]{def:phasetrans}\n    If, for a given infinite graph $G$ and fugacity $\\lambda>0$, there is only one hard-core measure on $G$ at fugacity $\\lambda$, then we say $G$ has \\emph{uniqueness} at $\\lambda$. If there are multiple such measures, we say that $G$ has \\emph{phase coexistence} at $\\lambda$.\n    If there exists some $\\lambda^*=\\lambda^*(G)$ such that $G$ has uniqueness for each $\\lambda < \\lambda^*$ and $G$ has phase coexistence for each $\\lambda>\\lambda^*$, then we say that a \\emph{phase transition} occurs at $\\lambda^*$, or more specifically that $\\lambda^*$ is the \\emph{Gibbs uniqueness threshold} for $G$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.795845+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ff91bb7a170547899a3b17eaa7ad9a11ddc947f90939d7baa4b872b5ddd0d1a0","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(\Lambda:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be finite, \(C^1\), and strictly convex,
and define
\[
        J(x):=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb R}\{\theta x-\Lambda(\theta)\},
        \qquad x\in\mathbb R.
\]
Set \(m_-:=\lim_{\theta\to-\infty}\Lambda'(\theta)\) and
\(m_+:=\lim_{\theta\to+\infty}\Lambda'(\theta)\), allowing infinite limits.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every \(x\in(m_-,m_+)\), the supremum defining \(J(x)\) is attained
at the unique \(\theta(x)\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\(\Lambda'(\theta(x))=x\), and
\[
J(x)=\theta(x)x-\Lambda(\theta(x)).
\]

\item The function \(J\) is differentiable on \((m_-,m_+)\), with
\(J'(x)=\theta(x)\). In particular, \(J\) is strictly convex on
\((m_-,m_+)\).

\item For every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\),
\(J(\Lambda'(\theta))=\theta\Lambda'(\theta)-\Lambda(\theta)\).

\item If \(\Lambda(0)=0\) and \(\Lambda'(0)\in(m_-,m_+)\), then
\(J(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), and \(J\) vanishes uniquely at
\(x=\Lambda'(0)\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Lebesgue measure on R^n","M is the centered or uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.553467+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, maximal functions","id":"claim_ffa8aee1191447b8b8fa930b110a55716c66233d776634ca4058ba7238a266e6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"The Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality is WEAK type (1,1), never strong type (1,1), and Marcinkiewicz interpolation gives nothing at p = 1 (its constant contains p/(p - p_0) and blows up as p -> 1+). Precisely: if f is in L^1(R^n) and f is not a.e. 0, then Mf is NOT in L^1(R^n). Global counterexample: pick R with c = int_{B(0,R)} |f| > 0; for |x| >= R the ball B(x, 2|x|) contains B(0,R), so Mf(x) >= c / (v_n (2|x|)^n), which is not integrable at infinity. Local counterexample showing the failure is not only at infinity: f(x) = |x|^{-n} (log(1/|x|))^{-2} 1_{{|x| < 1/2}} is in L^1, but averaging over B(x, 2|x|) gives Mf(x) >= c' |x|^{-n} (log(1/|x|))^{-1} near 0, which is not locally integrable. The correct endpoint substitutes are: (i) the weak (1,1) bound |{Mf > t}| <= 3^n ||f||_1 / t; (ii) Stein's L log L theorem: for f supported in a ball B, Mf is integrable over B if and only if int_B |f| log^+ |f| < infinity. So a proof that applies 'M is bounded on L^p' at p = 1, or that interpolates strong (1,1) with strong (infinity, infinity), is wrong; the same warning applies to any operator known only to be weak (1,1), such as the Calderon-Zygmund singular integrals and the Hilbert transform.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is locally integrable on R^n","balls are Euclidean and |.| is Lebesgue measure"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.552000+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, real-variable methods","id":"claim_ffa9201fa7a9c6fdbdafe36863b70b61b6ad169b72c4ec8441e19549baf37472","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For f in L^1_loc(R^n) (Lebesgue measure |.|), the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function is Mf(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/|B(x,r)|) int_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, with values in [0, infinity]. The uncentered version is M'f(x) = sup over all open balls B containing x of (1/|B|) int_B |f|; one has Mf <= M'f <= 2^n Mf. The set {Mf > t} is open for every t (so Mf is lower semicontinuous, hence Borel measurable), M is sublinear, M(f) = M(|f|), and ||Mf||_infinity <= ||f||_infinity. Cubes in place of balls give a pointwise comparable operator (constants depending only on n).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0131-recurrence-transience-dichotomy-for-excited-random-walks-in-dimension","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.048267+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ffe45b11bea72f88b0f33db0ab1140dd2a354730db9d40293fa198c173753b6c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare with the RWRE 0-1 law in d >= 3 (C0044) and locate the extra difficulty from self-interaction. Result: For Markovian RWRE the dichotomy question is the directional 0-1 law (C0044, open in d >= 3). For excited random walks the process is not Markov, and even the statement 'either recurrent or transient' (return to the origin infinitely often a.s. or finitely often a.s.) is not implied by any Markov-chain dichotomy; the source's Definition 3.1 asks for a 0-1 law for the number of returns. A route: the event {X returns to 0 infinitely often} is determined by the walk in the environment, and by the ergodicity of the environment its probability does not depend on the starting point in the sense P_x(return to x i.o.) is constant in x; but P_0(return to 0 i.o.) in (0,1) is not excluded by that. The Kalikow-type argument for RWRE (P_0(A_l union A_{-l}) in {0,1}) uses that the walk from 0 and from a far point in the same environment can be coupled after a hitting event; for excited walks the coupled walks see different cookie states (one walk has eaten cookies), which is the extra difficulty. Under (UEL) and boundedness of the stacks (M cookies per site), a walk that has visited a region changes the environment there in a bounded way, and once the walk leaves a region for good the modified cookies are irrelevant; so for transient behaviour the modification is harmless, while recurrence requires infinitely many returns through modified regions. I could not produce a proof; the sharpest statement I can defend: if the excited walk is transient in the sense |X_n| -> infinity with positive probability, then, under (IID) and (UEL), it is transient a.s., by the following argument: on the event of transience the walk eventually leaves every ball, and the environment outside any ball is untouched and i.i.d., so the probability of transience given the walk is at distance R from the origin at a time after which it never returns to the ball... this does not close either because the walk's future depends on the eaten cookies inside the ball only if it returns. Recorded as attempted without result. Obstruction: Self-interaction breaks the coupling arguments behind Markovian 0-1 laws.","status":"unverified"}
